content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm new to [product_name] [version_no]. I'm struggling to add the external module [product_name] [article_no] to my main PLC [product_name]. I'm unsure of the steps to take. When I try to add a device, I don't see modules like DI or DO available. How can I add [product_name] [article_no] to my hardware project? Do I need to download something? This small PLC is giving me a lot of trouble. Thanks in advance.

There isn't a hardware configuration like in [product_name] [version_no]. Expansion modules can't be added in the network view; only base modules with ethernet ports (masters, slaves, operator devices, etc.) can be added there. The program only lets you use the total number of inputs and outputs. The first DI on the initial digital expansion module is I9, the next is I10, and so forth. The first DO is Q5, followed by Q6, etc.

Thank you, [user_name]. It seems my electrician made a mistake. I have one CPU [product_name] [version_no] and four [product_name] [article_no]. The documentation says 'only 24DI and 16DO.' Maybe the problem is that I have too many external modules. Is that correct? Thanks!

A [product_name] [article_no] supports: DI = 24, DO = 20, AI = 8, AO = 8. You can connect up to two [product_name] [article_no] modules to a [product_name] [article_no] base module. The base module provides 8 DI and 4 DO; two additional [product_name] [article_no] modules add 16 DI and 16 DO, totaling 24 DI and 20 DO. If you haven't specified the base module model, here's some advice: You can't directly connect a [product_name] [article_no] module to a 230VAC base module; an analog expansion module must be placed between them.
Try using the TIA Selection Tool—it will guide you through the correct configuration.
Thank you for the help; it clarified my confusion. I had too many inputs and outputs. Another question: What is the TIA Selection Tool? I'm hearing about this software for the first time.
A new question from [user_name] has been moved to a separate thread titled 'What to do when run out of lines on the ladder diagram page?' Best regards [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users experienced difficulty identifying how to add external digital modules within [product_name] software, causing confusion especially for newcomers. The main pain points were understanding hardware restrictions and workflow differences compared to other [company_name] PLC environments. The interface does not clearly communicate module limits or configuration steps, leading to frustration for users familiar with more advanced systems expecting similar hardware management capabilities.
analysis.user_expectations: Users hope to have a simple, graphical way to add and configure external DI and DO modules. They expect clear notifications when hardware limits are met and want thorough documentation or built-in tools that provide direct guidance during setup.
